question.text: Sapphire Growth Fund (Cat II) had a net LONG-TERM CAPITAL LOSS of INR 12 crore in FY 2024-25. Under Sections 70-74 of the ITA and 115UB, how is this loss treated between the fund and its LPs?

answer.text: The loss is absorbed at fund level against future business income and cannot be passed through.
The loss is passed through only to resident LPs, not to non-residents.
The loss is forfeited at year-end and cannot be carried forward.
The loss is passed through to LPs who have held units for at least 12 months, to be set off only against their LTCG and, if unutilised, carried forward for 8 years.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115UB read with the general loss-set-off framework (Sec 70-74) allows non-business losses of a Cat I/II AIF to be passed through to LPs who have held the units for at least 12 months. LTCL can be set off only against LTCG (intra-head restriction under Sec 70/74), not against STCG or any other head. Unabsorbed LTCL carries forward in the LP's hands for 8 assessment years and retains its long-term character. The Trap: Option A confuses non-business loss with business loss — business loss is trapped at fund level; non-business loss passes through. Option C invents a residency-based filter which doesn't exist. Option D wrongly forfeits the loss instead of permitting carry-forward. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same loss-pass-through mechanics. XIX-A tests it at the distributor level — explaining to LPs why they need to hold units 12 months to claim the loss pass-through. XXI-B (PMS) is direct custody so loss treatment is native, not via pass-through. Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Manager, in years of net loss it is essential to issue Form 64C with loss break-up (LTCL / STCL / other) per LP. If an LP exits before 12 months, their loss share cannot be passed through — consider giving them an explicit note in the redemption statement so their CA doesn't wrongly claim it.
